Returns a step_up_token that records its tier (BR-ID-34): `tier=totp` with the current
authenticator code, `tier=sms` with the code sent by POST /admin/v1/auth/step-up/sms-codes.
The console sends the token as the `X-Step-Up-Token` request header of the admin
operation that answered 10003 and replays that request; the header is never put in the
body. An operation that needs the sms tier rejects a totp-tier token with 10003
`data.tier=sms`. Which tier each operation needs is annotated per permission in GET
/admin/v1/me/permissions (04 §11 step-up column).
`tier=sms` on an account without a registered verify phone is 10003 with `data.tier=sms`
and `data.reason=verify_phone_missing`. A wrong code is 20002 without a reason; an expired
or voided SMS code is 20003. Not fixed by BR-ID-34 and left open here: whether wrong
step-up codes count towards the login-failure lock, and the token lifetime and number of
uses (the response carries `expire_at`; the server decides).

`step_up_operations` lists the operations whose tier differs from it (e.g. only raising the

get.summary: The console workbench — to-do counts, yesterday's overview and system status
get.description:
Permission point `dashboard.view` (04 §11.1; read only, no step-up); without it the
operation is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied` and the console lands on the
first menu the account may open (01 F-ADM-26, 04 §6.6 dashboard). A super admin holds every
point. Read-only aggregate: nothing is written here, every card links to its own page.

The server trims the response to the account's permission points; the console renders only
what comes back (no greyed-out cards):
- `todo[]`: one entry per to-do card (`key`, enum admin_dashboard_todo_key) the account
  holds the card's point for — withdraw_review_pending `withdraw.review`,
  claim_review_pending `order.claim`, settle_bill_pending `settle.bill`, recon_diff_open
  `fund.recon`, appeal_pending `risk.appeal`, agent_report_overdue `agent.report`,
  beneficiary_held_overdue `risk.freeze`, union_auth_expiring `union.account_auth` (counting
  rules in the BR each enum value names). A card the account may see is returned with
  `count=0` when nothing is waiting (the card still shows). A card whose module has not
  shipped yet is left out exactly like a card without the point: the three fund cards
  (withdraw_review_pending, settle_bill_pending, recon_diff_open) appear once the fund
  line's console tasks ship. `route` is the console route the card opens, with its
  filter; `oldest_at` (optional, nullable) is the earliest waiting item's time;
  `breakdown` (optional) splits the count by a card-specific sub-key (for
  claim_review_pending `auto_matched` and `manual_review`); clients ignore keys they do
  not know.
- `yesterday`: always returned with `dashboard.view`. Yesterday's whole accounting day
  (`date`), aggregated daily with the report rules, not live (01 F-ADM-26 ②): `links`
  (link_logs created that day), `orders` (sub-orders with paid_at that day, not reduced by
  later invalidation), `est_rebate_fen` (users' share of those sub-orders still
  rebate_status=ESTIMATED and platform_status≠DEPOSIT_PAID at aggregation time, BR-TEXT-21),
  `new_users` (users registered that day); `as_of` is the aggregation time.
- `status`: only with `fund.view`, otherwise the whole object is absent: payout queue
  paused (`payout.queue_paused`), the payout channels paused one by one
  (`payout.channel_paused.<channel>`), monthly auto settlement (`settle.auto.enabled`) and
  whether the enterprise Alipay balance W is expired (BR-WDR-18; null until W entry ships
  with the fund line).
No open-alerts count is returned (alert records and closing rules are not defined yet;

get.summary: Search the audit log (own records, or everyone's with audit.view_all)
get.description:
Any signed-in admin account (no permission point needed, no step-up; 01 F-ADM-03, 04 §6.6
audit-logs). Records of the console's app, newest first (`at` descending, then the
server's internal order for the same time), page by page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200, above that 20001).
Visibility (04 §11.1 `audit.view_all`, enforced by the server, not by the console): an
account holding `audit.view_all` (a super admin holds every point) sees every account's
records and may filter by any `actor_id`; an account without it only sees its own records:
the server forces `actor_id` to the caller, so without `actor_id` it gets its own records
and with another account's `actor_id` it gets an empty page (`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an
error. An `actor_id` that names no account is an empty page as well.
Filters combine with AND: `actor_id` (the admin who acted), `target_type` and `target_id`
(exact match), `permission` (the permission point the action was done under), `from`
(inclusive) and `to` (exclusive), ISO 8601 times with offset (04 §5); `from` later than
`to` is 20001 with `data.fields=[from, to]`. `target_type`, `target_id` and `permission`
are derived by the server from the stored record (the action and its target); a record
they cannot be derived for (older rows, actions without an object) returns them as null
and never matches a filter on that field. `target_type` is free text, not an enum.
Each row has the actor's current username (`actor_name`, null when the account is gone),
never the before / after values (GET /admin/v1/audit-logs/{id}). Searching does not write
an audit record itself.

caller (another value → empty page).

parameters.name: target_id
parameters.description: Object id of the record (exact match), such as a user_id.

parameters.description: Permission point the action was done under (enum admin_permission).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Earliest record time, inclusive (ISO 8601 with offset).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Latest record time, exclusive (ISO 8601 with offset).

audit-logs). Same fields as a list row plus `before` and `after`: the stored values as
written by the action (any JSON, null when the action recorded none; sensitive fields are
stored masked, so they are shown masked). Without `audit.view_all` (04 §11.1) only the
caller's own records are found: another account's record is 20001 with `data.fields=[id]`,
the same as an unknown id or a record of another app (no probing). Reading a record does
not write an audit record itself.

post.summary: Create an export task from a list's filters (asynchronous CSV, masked by default)
post.description:
Permission point `export` (04 §11.1) and, in addition, the permission of the source list
itself (enum export_resource: `users` needs `user.list`; `audit_logs` needs no more than
being signed in); lacking either is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. The
task is generated asynchronously as one CSV file in a private object-storage bucket
(BR-ID-34 细则「后台导出任务」); the response is 202 with the new task in status pending.
Each call creates a new task (no Idempotency-Key, 04 §6.6).
`filters` has the same shape as the query parameters of the source list (paging excluded)
and is judged like them: `users` takes `risk_state` (GET /admin/v1/users); `audit_logs`
takes `actor_id`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `permission`, `from`, `to` (GET
/admin/v1/audit-logs; `from` later than `to` is 20001 with `data.fields=[from, to]`, as on
the list). The file holds the rows the source list would
show for these filters to the creator, with the list's columns. An `audit_logs` export
applies the same own-records rule as the list (04 §11.1 `audit.view_all`): without
`audit.view_all` the server forces `actor_id` to the creator, and another account's
`actor_id` gives an empty file (status done, `row_count=0`), not an error.
Masking: by default every export is masked like its source list (the phone number 3 + 4,
BR-ID-33) and the task has `masked=true`. Only a `users` export may ask for the full values
with `unmasked: true`; then the creator must hold `pii.reveal_phone` (the users list's only
sensitive column; otherwise 10403), send a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` (the tier of
`pii.reveal_phone`; missing, expired or lower → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`) and give
`reason` (1–200 characters; missing → 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`). `reason` without
`unmasked: true` is 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`; an `audit_logs` request takes
neither field (audit values are stored masked) and either one is 20001. Without
`unmasked: true` no step-up token is needed and none is checked.
Audit (BR-ID-34): creating writes an audit record (action export_create: task id, resource,
filters, masked). An unmasked task writes its own audit record as well (action
export_unmasked: task id, resource, reason and, once generated, the row count; never a
value).
Limits are configuration keys whose default values the implementation sets:
`admin.export.max_rows` (rows per file; a task with more rows fails with a failure_reason
saying so, narrow the filters) and `admin.export.max_running_per_admin` (tasks of one
creator generated at the same time; the rest stay pending until a slot frees up).
Lifecycle (enum export_status): pending → running → done or failed; done → expired 24
hours after the file was generated (BR-ID-30 ⑨, the object-storage lifecycle rule deletes
the file); pending or running → cancelled when the creator's account is disabled (with an
audit record); failed → pending by POST /admin/v1/exports/{id}/retry. There is no cancel
operation.

`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Tasks of the console's app, newest first
(`created_at` descending, then the server's internal order for the same time), page by page
(`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200, above that 20001).
Visibility (enforced by the server, BR-ID-34 细则「后台导出任务」): an account holding
`audit.view_all` (a super admin holds every point) sees every account's tasks, their
filters summary and status; an account without it only sees the tasks it created.
`audit.view_all` only widens this list: downloading and retrying stay limited to the
creator (GET /admin/v1/exports/{id}/download, POST /admin/v1/exports/{id}/retry).
Filters combine with AND: `status` (enum export_status), `resource` (enum
export_resource), `from` (inclusive) and `to` (exclusive) on `created_at`, ISO 8601 times
with offset (04 §5); `from` later than `to` is 20001 with `data.fields=[from, to]`.
Rows never carry the download link; status names come from BR-TEXT-25
admin_dict.export_status. Listing does not write an audit record.

get.summary: Get a short-lived signed link to the file of one's own finished export (audited)
get.description:
Permission point `export` (04 §11.1; no step-up); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Only the creator of the task can download it, even
with `audit.view_all` (BR-ID-34 细则「后台导出任务」). Every call is authorized again and
signs a new link; no long-lived link is issued. The server also checks that the creator
still holds the permission of the source list (`users` → `user.list`) and, for an unmasked
file (`masked=false`), still holds the pii point it was made under (`pii.reveal_phone`).
Another account's task, an unknown id, a task of another app, and a creator who no longer
holds those points are all 20001 with `data.fields=[id]` (no probing).
Only a task in status done whose `expires_at` has not passed can be downloaded; any other
status is 30417 with `data.status` (pending, running, failed, expired, cancelled; a done
task past `expires_at` answers expired even before the server has set the status).
The link `url` is valid until `url_expires_at` = min(5 minutes from now, the task's
`expires_at`), so a disabled or demoted creator loses access within minutes.
Every call that returns a link writes its own audit record (action export_download: task
id, resource, masked; never the link) before the response is sent. The response carries
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: Retry one's own failed export task
post.description:
Permission point `export` (04 §11.1); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Only the creator of the task can retry it, even with
`audit.view_all`: another account's task, an unknown id or a task of another app is 20001
with `data.fields=[id]` (no probing; BR-ID-34 细则「后台导出任务」).
Only a failed task can be retried; any other status is 30417 with `data.status` (pending,
running, done, expired, cancelled; the same code as a download in the wrong status).
The checks of creating are made again on the caller's current points: the permission of
the source list (`users` → `user.list`) and, for an unmasked task (`masked=false`),
`pii.reveal_phone`, both 10403 when lacking. An unmasked task also needs a new totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` (missing, expired or lower → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`) and a new
`reason` (1–200 characters; missing → 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`): every
generation of a file with full values is verified anew. A masked task takes an empty body;
`reason` there is 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]` and no step-up token is checked.
The task keeps its id, resource, filters and masked flag and goes back to pending
(`progress`, `failure_reason` cleared); the response is the task as it is now. Retrying
writes an audit record (action export_retry: task id, resource, masked), and an unmasked
task its own record with the new reason (action export_unmasked). No Idempotency-Key
(04 §6.6): a second call while the task is pending again is 30417.

get.description:
Permission point `user.list` (04 §11.1; read only, no step-up); without it the console can
only look users up one by one through GET /admin/v1/users/lookup (`user.lookup`), and this
list is 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Users of the console's app, newest
registration first, page by page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200), optionally filtered by

(`138****5678`, BR-ID-33) and the full number is only shown through POST
/admin/v1/users/{user_id}/reveal; no identity number, payout account, real name or raw
risk reason. Balances, orders and withdrawals of a user are not part of this contract yet.

get.summary: Top-bar search by a full order number, withdrawal number, phone number or UID
get.description:
The console's top-bar search (01 F-ADM-04; 04 §6.6 search; BR-ID-34 细则「一框搜」). Any
signed-in admin may call it (read only, no step-up); what comes back is trimmed by the
server to three permission points, one per hit type (enum admin_search_hit_type): order
`order.view`, user `user.lookup`, withdrawal `fund.view`. A super admin holds every point.

`q` is trimmed of surrounding whitespace and must then be 1–64 characters, else 20001 with
`data.fields=[q]`. The server tells from its shape what `q` is and matches the full value
only (no prefix or partial match): an order number (the order's full number), a withdrawal
number (its full number; no hit until the withdrawal module ships), a full phone number
(normalised as in BR-ID-05 细则「手机号规范化」) or a UID (the user_id, a UUID). Only
objects of the console's app are found. Input of no recognised shape is not an error: 200
with an empty list.

Anti-probing (BR-ID-34 细则「一框搜」): no hit and no permission look the same. A hit of a
type the account has no point for is dropped silently; when nothing is left the response is
200 with `items=[]` and `truncated=false`. The operation never answers 10403
`admin_permission_denied` (10403 only for `admin_ip_not_allowed`, common to every admin
operation) and never 20001 for an unknown number, unlike GET /admin/v1/users/lookup.

`items[]` lists the hits (`type`, `id` for the detail route, `summary` a masked one-line
summary: phone numbers masked 3 + 4 as BR-ID-33, no full phone, identity or payout account
number). An order or withdrawal hit is followed by its owner as a `user` item, trimmed by
`user.lookup` like any user hit. At most 10 items; when there are more, the first 10 come
back with `truncated=true` (the console asks for a more complete number). The console
opens the detail page directly when exactly one item comes back and lists candidates
otherwise.

Audit: a search by full phone number that returns a user writes an audit entry, as a
lookup by phone through `user.lookup` does (04 §6.6 search). Other searches are not
audited.

valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). An unknown `user_id`
is 20001 with `data.fields=[user_id]`.
Body checks (20001 with `data.fields` naming the field): `reason` is required (1–200
characters); `reason_category` (enum risk_reason_category, BR-TEXT-23 细则「原因类别」) is
required for `ban` and `freeze` and not accepted for `unban` and `unfreeze`;
`frozen_until` is only accepted for `freeze`, null or absent means a freeze without end
(BR-ID-36), and a value must be later than the server's current time (no upper bound).

normal or frozen (on a frozen user it rewrites `frozen_until`, `reason_category` and
`reason`); `unban` only from banned; `unfreeze` only from frozen. A banned user is not
frozen directly (unban first); an appealing user is refused for every action, the appeal
is concluded through the appeal console instead (BR-ID-36).

means "the console saw no risk-state row" and only creates the user's first row while
there is still none; an integer only matches the row's current `row_version`. Every other

while there is no row, or an integer other than the current one. State rules are judged

invalid (the user authorizes again), a binding on any other platform (such as pdd, which
has no re-authorization) becomes active and takes effect at once (BR-ID-20). `freeze` and
`unfreeze` touch neither sessions nor bindings
(withdrawals 30303 and held credits follow from the state, BR-WDR-05, BR-CALC-13); a

record (action user_risk_state_change, before and after state, reason category and
reason). After the risk state changes, the notification module sends the in-app message
RISK_STATE_CHANGED (BR-TEXT-23; a ban notice becomes visible only after the unban,
BR-ID-31); this operation does not send it and its response does not wait for the
sending. The response is the risk state as it is now. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

get.summary: Order claims to review (filters, page by page, a count per claim status)
get.description:
The claim review list (01 F-ADM-06; 04 §6.6 claims; BR-ATTR-18). Read only, no step-up.
Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2) reads every claim of the console's app. An
account holding only `user.lookup` (04 §11.1: it may see the claims of a user it looks up)
may read the list only together with `user_id`, the user detail page's claims tab
(design/specs/admin-user-detail.md); without `user_id` that account gets 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`, the same as an account holding neither point. A
super admin holds every point. Approving and rejecting stay with `order.claim` alone
(CT-24l).

Filters combine with AND: `platform`, `evidence_level` (enum claim_evidence_level, the
claim's level, that is its weakest child order), `status` (enum claim_status), `user_id`
(the applicant; the user filter takes the user_id only: UID and phone number go through
the top-bar search GET /admin/v1/search, not this list) and `q`. `q` is trimmed of
surrounding whitespace and spaces inside are removed, then it must be 1–64 characters,
else 20001 with `data.fields=[q]`; it matches exactly (no prefix or partial match) a
claim_id (the display number of a claim is its claim_id; there is no separate claim
number), the order number as submitted, or the number of one of the claim's child
orders. A `user_id` that names no user of the app, or a filter set nothing matches, is an
empty page (`items=[]`, `total=0`), not an error; `counts` still follows its own rule
below (every filter except `status`), so a `status` nothing matches leaves the other
counts as they are (a user with 3 approved claims and none rejected, read with
`status=rejected`: `items=[]`, `total=0`, `counts.approved=3`), and every count is 0 only
when the filters other than `status` match nothing. A value outside an enum is 20001 with
`data.fields` naming the parameter.

Order: claims with status `auto_matched` first (BR-ATTR-18: kept at the top for the
reviewer), then every other claim; within each group `submitted_at` descending, then the
server's internal order for the same time. Pages with `page` (any positive integer, as
AdminPage; a page past the last one is `items=[]`) and `page_size` ≤ 200 (a `page_size`
above 200 is 20001, as AdminPageSize). `counts` has one entry per claim_status value (0 included), counted with
every filter of the request except `status`, so the console's status tabs show what each
tab would hold; `total` is the count of the page's own filter set. The applicant is shown
as user_id and phone number masked 3 + 4 (BR-ID-33), never the full number. Reading does
not write an audit record.

200.description: One page of claims, auto_matched first, then newest submitted first, with a count per status.

get.summary: One claim with its child orders and the evidence view
get.description:
The claim review page (01 F-ADM-06; 04 §6.6 claims; BR-ATTR-18). Read only, no step-up.
Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2) reads any claim of the console's app. An account
holding only `user.lookup` (04 §11.1) must pass `user_id` (the user it is looking at);
without it the account gets 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`, the same as
an account holding neither point. When `user_id` is given (by any account) and the claim's
applicant is another user, the answer is 20001 with `data.fields=[claim_id]`, the same as
an unknown claim_id or a claim of another app (no probing). The display number of a claim
is its claim_id.

Same fields as a list row plus `reason` (the note of the latest approval or rejection,
claims.reason, null before any; every note is kept in the audit log) and `items`, one per child order (claim_items): its own evidence level (BR-ATTR-18 counts per
child order, for the applicant only), the decision (null while pending), the reject reason
(enum claim_reject_reason, set with a rejection only), when and by whom it was decided
(`decided_by` null for a decision made by the system: a NOT_IN_POOL or ORDER_INVALID
rejection or a cancellation after attribution by sync), the reviewer's display name
(`decided_by_name`: admin_users.display_name, the username when that is empty, null when
`decided_by` is null or the account is gone), the `row_version` that the approve and
reject operations take as `expected_row_version` (CT-24l), `matches` and `evidence_links`.
`matches` compares, field by field, what the user submitted with what the union reported
for that child order (enum admin_claim_match_field: order number, payment date; for a
pre-sale order the union side is the date the deposit was paid), values as strings in the
contract's formats, with the server's verdict in `matched`. `evidence_links` lists the
link records that count as the child order's evidence (BR-ATTR-18: the applicant's own
convert and open records with result_code 0 inside the window before the child order's
attribution time, newest first), each with its time and scene only: no product, shop,
promotion or raw union data. It is empty for evidence `none`. Reading does not write an
audit record.

post.summary: Approve one child order of a claim (returns the whole claim after the review)
post.description:
Approves one child order (claim_items) of a claim (01 F-ADM-06; 04 §6.6 claims; BR-ATTR-18,
BR-ATTR-20). Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2) only: an account holding only
`user.lookup`, or neither, gets 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied` (a super
admin holds every point). No step-up. No Idempotency-Key: the console's writes rely on the
CAS below (04 §6.6). One child order per call; there is no batch approval.

Request: `expected_row_version` is the child order's `row_version` from
GET /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}. `reason` is required for approval and rejection alike,
5–200 characters (the console may prefill 「证据核实一致」); after trimming surrounding
whitespace it must still have at least 5 characters, else 20001 with
`data.fields=[reason]`; it is stored trimmed. An unknown claim_id or a claim of another
app → 20001 with `data.fields=[claim_id]`; an unknown item_id, or one that belongs to
another claim → 20001 with `data.fields=[item_id]`. A child order that is already decided
(approved, rejected or cancelled, by a reviewer or by the system, such as sync
attribution closing it under BR-ATTR-16), or whose `row_version` is no longer
`expected_row_version` → 20902 with `data.resource=claim_item`, nothing changed; the
console refreshes and shows the result.

Approval runs in one transaction under BR-ATTR-20: it takes
pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(platform, sub_order_id)), the same lock as sync and admin
assignment (BR-ATTR-01), re-reads the order with SELECT … FOR UPDATE, and then checks in
this order (BR-ATTR-20 ② before ③):
- The order's user_id is no longer empty (attributed by sync, by another claim or by an
  admin assignment): the order is not written and no commission snapshot is made; the
  child order is closed as BR-ATTR-16 says, `cancelled` when that user_id is the
  applicant, else `rejected` with `reject_reason=NOT_IN_POOL`. This is not an error: the
  answer is 200 with the claim as it is after closing. Signal (no extra field): the
  reviewed child order's `decision` in the response. A request to approve whose child
  order comes back `cancelled`, or `rejected` with NOT_IN_POOL, was closed this way, and
  the console tells the reviewer 「订单已被自动归属」.
- Else the order's rebate_status is VOID: the system rejects the child order with
  `reject_reason=ORDER_INVALID` (BR-ATTR-18; a claim never takes a VOID order,
  BR-ATTR-17 ④c, BR-ATTR-20 ③), again 200 with the claim; the order is not written.
- Else the child order becomes `approved` and the order is attributed to the applicant
  as BR-ATTR-20 ③ says: user_id, user_basis=claim, locked=true, platform_status
  unchanged, rebate_status out of UNATTRIBUTED by BR-FUND-01 R3, the commission snapshot
  under the conditions of BR-ATTR-01 ⑥, order_status_history with source=claim, the
  domain event claim.resolved queued in the same transaction, and source backfill
  (BR-ATTR-15). Every other pending child order of the same sub order (in claims of other
  applicants) is rejected with NOT_IN_POOL in the same transaction (BR-ATTR-18: the first
  approval wins).
A child order closed by the system (`cancelled`, NOT_IN_POOL, ORDER_INVALID) has
`decided_by` null, as GET /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id} describes; an approval has the
reviewer.

In every outcome the child order's `row_version` goes up by 1 and `decided_at` is set,
`reason` is written to claims.reason (the latest note, shown as the claim's `reason`) and
to the audit log together with the operator and the outcome; child orders have no note
of their own. When every child order of the claim is decided, the claim's `status` is
summarized (BR-ATTR-18: any approved → approved; else any rejected → rejected; else
cancelled); while one is pending it stays as it is. The applicant is told the result by
in-app message and push (BR-ATTR-18). The response is the whole claim after the review,
the same shape as GET /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}.

200.description: The whole claim after the review (approved, or closed by the system).

approved.summary: The child order is approved; every child order is decided, so the claim is approved

autoAttributed.summary: The order was attributed to another user meanwhile; the child order is closed with NOT_IN_POOL (console shows 「订单已被自动归属」)

post.summary: Reject one child order of a claim with a reviewer reject reason (returns the whole claim)
post.description:
Rejects one child order (claim_items) of a claim (01 F-ADM-06; 04 §6.6 claims;
BR-ATTR-18). Permission point `order.claim` (04 §11.2) only: an account holding only
`user.lookup`, or neither, gets 10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. No
step-up and no Idempotency-Key (CAS, 04 §6.6). One child order per call; there is no
batch rejection.

Request: `expected_row_version`, `reason` and the errors for them, for an unknown
claim_id or item_id and for a decided or changed child order are the same as
POST /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}/items/{item_id}/approve (`reason` 5–200 characters,
else 20001 with `data.fields=[reason]`; 20902 with `data.resource=claim_item`).
`reject_reason` takes only the six codes a reviewer may choose (BR-ATTR-18): NO_EVIDENCE,
EXPIRED_CLICK (the applicant only has records of the same product older than 360 hours),
NOT_TRACKED, OTHER_TLJ, FRAUD, OTHER. NOT_IN_POOL and ORDER_INVALID are set by the system
only; sending one of them, or any other value → 20001 with `data.fields=[reject_reason]`.

Rejection runs in one transaction: it takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(platform,
sub_order_id)), the same lock as approval, sync and admin assignment (BR-ATTR-01), re-reads
the order with SELECT … FOR UPDATE, and then:
- The order's rebate_status is VOID: the system rejects the child order with
  `reject_reason=ORDER_INVALID` (BR-ATTR-18: an order already void at review is rejected
  by the system, whether the reviewer pressed approve or reject; approval does the same),
  not with the reviewer's `reject_reason`, and `decided_by` is null (a system decision,
  as in approval). This is not an error: the answer is 200 with the claim. Signal (no
  extra field): the reviewed child order comes back with `reject_reason=ORDER_INVALID`.
- Else the child order becomes `rejected` with that `reject_reason` and `decided_by` the
  reviewer.
In both outcomes `decided_at` is set and `row_version` goes up by 1; the order itself is
not written. `reason` is written to claims.reason (the latest note) and to the audit log
with the operator, the reject reason the reviewer chose and the outcome (including
ORDER_INVALID). When every child order is decided the claim's `status` is
summarized as BR-ATTR-18 says (any approved → approved; else any rejected → rejected;
else cancelled); while one is pending it stays as it is. The applicant is told the result
by in-app message and push (BR-ATTR-18). The response is the whole claim after the
review, the same shape as GET /admin/v1/claims/{claim_id}.

post.description:
Permission point `content.platform_icon`. Saves the cleaned file of an upload (POST
/admin/v1/platform-icons/{key}/uploads) as the next version of the mark (versions are
counted per mark from 1). Nothing is published: the version takes effect only through
POST /admin/v1/platform-icons/{key}/publish. When the upload has `sanitized=true` the
operator must have looked at the cleaned preview and `sanitized_confirmed` must be true,
otherwise 20001 with `data.fields=[sanitized_confirmed]` (BR-TEXT-24 细则「已清除不安全内容」).
`source_url` (the official brand or asset download page) and `downloaded_on` may be left
out: such a version is a draft (`publishable=false`) until both are registered with PATCH
/admin/v1/platform-icons/{key}/versions/{version} (BR-TEXT-24 细则「必填登记」). Saving
is naturally idempotent: an upload_id this mark has already saved as a version (a retry
after a lost response) returns 200 with that existing version as it is now, creates no
second version and applies nothing else from the retried body. An upload_id that does not
exist, has expired or belongs to another key is 20001 with `data.fields=[upload_id]`. No
Idempotency-Key: admin writes rely on these checks and on CAS where state is replaced
(04 §6.6).

post.description: Permission point `content.platform_icon`. `multipart/form-data` with one part `file`: an SVG, or a PNG with a transparent background and sides of at least 512 px, at most `content.platform_icon.max_bytes` bytes (default 204800; BR-TEXT-24 细则「上传与发布」). The server first converts an SVG faithfully (in-document `use` expanded, simple style declarations rewritten as presentation attributes), then cleans it against the whitelist; the result is stored in the OSS media bucket under its content SHA-256 and returned as `url` for an `` preview on light and dark backgrounds at 16, 24 and 32 px. Nothing is saved as a version yet (POST /admin/v1/platform-icons/{key}/versions takes the `upload_id` until `expires_at`). `sanitized=true` means the cleaned file differs from the original: the console shows 「已清除不安全内容」 and the operator confirms the preview before saving. post.description:
Permission point `content.platform_icon`. Makes `version` the published image of the mark
at once, with no gradual rollout (BR-TEXT-24 细则「发布与回滚」); the next GET /v1/config
lists it in `platform_icons` with the version's cleaned file url, its SHA-256 and the
version number (ConfigPlatformIcon). Publishing a version older than the current one is a
rollback; both are written to the audit log (action publish or rollback). CAS:
`expected_revision` is the mark's `revision` the console showed. The revision only ever
grows (every publish, rollback and restore-builtin adds 1), so a stale request, including
a retry of one that already took effect, never matches again: a mismatch → 20902 with
`data.resource=platform_icon`, refresh and retry (04 §6.6). Publishing the version that is
already current with a matching revision succeeds without change, revision bump or audit.
A version missing source registrations is 20001 with `data.fields` listing every missing
one (`[source_url]`, `[downloaded_on]`, or `[source_url, downloaded_on]` when both are
missing); an unknown version is 20001 with `data.fields=[version]`.

publish.summary: First replacement image over the built-in one

200.description: The mark with its new published version.

post.summary: Restore the built-in image of a platform mark
post.description:
Permission point `content.platform_icon`. 「恢复内置」 (BR-TEXT-24 细则「发布与回滚」): the
mark has no published version any more, the next GET /v1/config leaves its key out of
`platform_icons` and clients show the bundled image; saved versions are kept and can be
published again. Written to the audit log (action restore_builtin). CAS as in publish:
`expected_revision` is the mark's `revision` the console showed, the restore adds 1 to it,
and a mismatch → 20902 with `data.resource=platform_icon`. Restoring a mark that already
shows the built-in image (with a matching revision) succeeds without change, revision
bump or audit.

200.description: The mark, now on its built-in image.

get.summary: Configured pages with their released and gray versions
get.description:
Permission point `content.page` (04 §11.2; step-up 「–」). One row per page that has at
least one saved version (`home`, `custom:*`), ordered by page_key, page by page (`page`,
`page_size` ≤ 200): the fully released version, the gray version and its percentage, the
newest saved version, who changed the page last and when, and the page's `revision`, the
CAS value of every page write (04 §6.6 `pages`; 编排者默认).

get.summary: One configured page
get.description:
Permission point `content.page`. The page's released and gray versions, newest saved
version, last change and `revision` (the CAS value of every page write). A page_key of the
right shape with no saved version → 30701.

get.summary: Version history of one page
get.description:
Permission point `content.page`. Every saved version of the page, newest first, page by
page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200), drafts and rolled-back versions included, without their
sections (read one version for those). render_count and error_count stay 0 until the
render report of TECH-29 exists (编排者默认). A page_key of the right shape with no saved
version → 30701.

200.description: One page of versions, newest first.

post.summary: Save a draft as a new version of one page
post.description:
Permission point `content.page`. Saves `sections` as a new draft version (number = newest
version + 1, counted per page from 1); a saved version's content never changes again, so a
preview token stays pinned to what it shows (编排者默认). The first save creates the page.
Nothing is published: the draft takes effect only through POST
/admin/v1/pages/{page_key}/publish. Saving runs the same checks as publishing (04 §6.6):
jump targets (an ExternalPage url whose host is in the `union_host` category of the
platform link-pattern table while switch `external_page.union_host_block` is on, BR-ATTR-29
①; personal-data placeholders in an external url, BR-ID-33 细则「外链不带个人数据」;
Withdraw, PayoutAccount, LaborAgreement or RealName with params, BR-WDR-01 细则), the
notice_bar api data source (only the notice CMS, 03 §6.3) and union_material channels (only
selectable channels of specs/material-channels.yaml, BR-TEXT-17 细则「联盟物料频道」); a
failure is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the offending field as a dotted path with array
indexes (e.g. `sections.0.data_source`), no `data.reason` (编排者默认). CAS:
`expected_revision` is the page's `revision` the console showed, 0 for a page not saved
yet; saving adds 1, and a mismatch → 20902 with `data.resource=page` (编排者默认: drafts
are whole pages, so two editors must not save over each other unseen).

get.summary: One version of a page with its sections
get.description:
Permission point `content.page`. One saved version with its sections as stored. A
page_key of the right shape with no saved version, or a version the page does not have →
30701.

post.summary: Publish a draft version of a page (full or gray)
post.description:
Permission point `content.page`. Publishes the draft `version` after the same checks as
saving a draft (20001 with `data.fields` as a dotted path, see POST
/admin/v1/pages/{page_key}/versions). `gray_percent` 100 makes it the fully released
version (the previous one stays published but is no longer current); 1..99 makes it the
gray version, served to devices whose bucket is below gray_percent×100 (OPS-05); 0 is not
accepted, a gray version is stopped by rolling it back (编排者默认). Edges (编排者默认): a
page without a fully released version accepts only 100, otherwise 20001 with
`data.fields=[gray_percent]`; while a gray version exists no other version can be
published, 20001 with `data.fields=[version]` (release it fully or roll it back first); a
version that does not exist or is not a draft is 20001 with `data.fields=[version]`. CAS:
`expected_revision` is the page's `revision` the console showed; publishing adds 1, so a
stale request, including a retry of one that already took effect, never matches again: a
mismatch → 20902 with `data.resource=page`. A page with no saved version → 30701. Written
to the audit log.

200.description: The page with its new released or gray version.

post.summary: Change the gray percentage of a page, or release the gray version fully
post.description:
Permission point `content.page`. Sets the gray percentage of the page's gray version
(1..99), or with 100 releases it fully: the gray version becomes the fully released
version and the page has no gray version any more (编排者默认). A page without a gray
version is 20001 with `data.fields=[gray_percent]`. CAS as in publish: `expected_revision`
is the page's `revision` the console showed, the change adds 1, and a mismatch → 20902
with `data.resource=page`. A page with no saved version → 30701. Written to the audit
log.

widen.summary: Widen the gray version to half of the devices

release.summary: Release the gray version to everyone

200.description: The page with its new gray percentage or released version.

post.summary: Roll back the gray or the fully released version of a page
post.description:
Permission point `content.page`. `version` must be the page's current gray version or
current fully released version, otherwise 20001 with `data.fields=[version]` (编排者默认).
Rolling back the gray version marks it rolled_back and leaves the page without a gray
version. Rolling back the fully released version (only while there is no gray version,
otherwise 20001 with `data.fields=[version]`) marks it rolled_back and makes the published
version with the latest publish_at among the page's other published versions the fully
released one (ties: higher version); without one → 20001 with `data.fields=[version]`
(version numbers are save order, not publish order). Nothing is republished under a new
number: the version numbers clients saw stay as they were. CAS as in publish: `expected_revision` is the page's
`revision` the console showed, the rollback adds 1, and a mismatch → 20902 with
`data.resource=page`. A page with no saved version → 30701. Written to the audit log.

post.summary: Issue a preview token for one version of a page
post.description:
Permission point `content.page` (「草稿预览二维码」, TECH-11). Issues a read-only preview
token for `version`, in any status (编排者默认), valid 10 minutes and only in the
environment that issued it; the test build's HomePreview route reads the version with it
through GET /v1/pages/{page_key}/preview. The console draws the QR code from `token` and
`page_key` only, with no host name (03 §3.6); no deep link is returned (编排者默认). A
version the page does not have is 20001 with `data.fields=[version]`; a page with no saved
version → 30701. Written to the audit log.

get.summary: Published versions of the privacy policy, user agreement and labor agreement
get.description:
Permission point `content.agreement` (04 §11.2; read only, no step-up). Every published
version, newest first (by published_at), page by page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200),
optionally of one `type`; without the text (read one version for its title and body).
Published versions never change and are never deleted (04 §6.2).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only versions of this type; absent = all three types.

200.description: One page of published versions, newest first.

items.legal_confirm_note: 劳务协议第 2 版需重签

post.summary: Publish a new version of an agreement
post.description:
Permission point `content.agreement` (04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up: totp tier for every publish (without a
valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`; 04 §11.2 动态码, OPS-14).
The version number is the type's current newest version + 1 (1 for the first), set by the
server. `title` and `body` (tiptap JSON as a string, nodes and marks within the agreement
body whitelist) are the text; `min_version` is where re-consent (privacy, agreement,
BR-ID-12) or re-signing (labor_agreement, BR-WDR-31) starts; `legal_confirmed_by`,
`legal_confirm_note` and `legal_confirmed_on` record the legal confirmation (OPS-14,
BR-ID-12). A failed check is 20001 with `data.fields` naming the field: min_version below
the current version's min_version or above the new version, requires_resign not as the
publish rules require for the type and min_version, a legal confirmation field missing or
blank, or a body outside the whitelist. CAS: `expected_version` is the type's newest
version as the console showed it (0 when none is published yet); a mismatch → 20902 with
`data.resource=agreement`, refresh and retry (04 §6.6). In one transaction the server
inserts the agreement article (category agreement) and the agreements row, and for
privacy and agreement also writes legal.<type>.version (privacy also
legal.privacy.min_version, 04 §10.1). Writes an audit record with the legal confirmer,
the confirmation date and min_version and requires_resign before and after (BR-ID-12).
Published versions are never changed or deleted. The response is the new version. No
Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6; the CAS keeps a retry from publishing twice).

get.description:

data.title: 隐私政策

get.summary: Articles of the CMS (help, rules, notices, agreements)
get.description:
Permission point `content.article` (04 §11.2; step-up 「–」). One row per article, newest
`updated_at` first, page by page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200): category, the title, number
and status of the newest version row, the current version (the largest version whose status
is exactly published and whose published_at is not later than now, 04 §6.2; null when
there is none) with its published_at, and the article's `row_version`, the CAS value of
every article write. `category` filters by category; `status` filters by the status of
the newest version row (编排者默认). Articles of category agreement are listed read-only;
they are written through /admin/v1/agreements.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Status of the newest version row.

200.description: One page of articles, newest updated_at first.

post.summary: Create an article as a first draft
post.description:
Permission point `content.article`. Creates an article with the client-generated
`article_id` (a UUIDv7 the console generates once per new article and reuses on every retry
of that create; lowercase canonical form) and version 1 in status draft; nothing is
published. Admin writes carry no Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6), so the id is what makes a retry
safe: retrying the same article_id never creates a second article — when an article with
that id already exists → 20902 with `data.resource=article` and nothing is written; the
console then reads it back with GET /admin/v1/articles/{article_id} (编排者默认). An
article_id that is not a lowercase canonical UUIDv7 → 20001 `data.fields=[article_id]`,
checked before the save checks. Category
agreement is refused with 20001 `data.fields=[category]` (agreements are written through
/admin/v1/agreements). Save checks (04 §6.6 articles, shared by create, draft and
publish): an empty title or a title hitting the forbidden-word list (BR-TEXT-12 细则); a
body that is not a tiptap JSON document within the allowed node and mark list; a link
href that is not an https external link (App-internal links are not supported in this
batch, 编排者默认), whose host is in the `union_host` category of the platform
link-pattern table while switch `external_page.union_host_block` is on (BR-ATTR-29 ①), or
that carries a personal-data placeholder (BR-ID-33 细则「外链不带个人数据」); a notice
that cannot be closed without notice_end_at (BR-TEXT-13 细则「生效区间」) → 20001.
`data.fields` lists, in this order, the offending field names (title, body,
notice_end_at), the forbidden words hit and the JSON paths inside the body written as
`body.content[i]…` (编排者默认); no other data key. For categories other than notice the
notice fields are ignored and stored as notice_closable=true, notice_end_at=null
(编排者默认). notice_content_version is maintained by the server on save, never sent by
the console (BR-TEXT-13 细则「首页公告条的关闭与内容版本」). Written to the audit log in the
same transaction.

200.description: The new article with its first draft version.

get.summary: One article with all its versions
get.description:
Permission point `content.article`. The article with every version row, newest first,
drafts and offline versions included, each with its body, and the article's `row_version`
(the CAS value of every article write). current_version is the largest version whose
status is exactly published and whose published_at is not later than now (a scheduled
version not yet due does not count), null when there is none (04 §6.2). An article_id
that is not a lowercase canonical UUID, or that does not exist → 30701.

put.summary: Save a new draft version of an article
put.description:
Permission point `content.article`. Inserts a new version row (newest version + 1) in
status draft with the given title, body and notice fields; a saved version's body is never
changed in place (编排者默认). Same save checks and `data.fields` as POST
/admin/v1/articles. An article of category agreement → 20001 `data.fields=[category]`.
CAS: `expected_row_version` is the article's `row_version` the console showed; the new
row takes the previous newest row's row_version + 1, and a mismatch → 20902 with
`data.resource=article` (编排者默认). An article_id that is not a lowercase canonical UUID,
or that does not exist → 30701. Written to the audit log in the same transaction.

200.description: The article with its new draft version.

post.summary: Publish the newest draft version of an article, now or at a set time
post.description:
Permission point `content.article`. Publishes `version`, which must be the article's
newest version and in status draft, otherwise 20001 `data.fields=[version]` (older drafts
stay draft, 编排者默认). `published_at` defaults to the server's current time; a time
earlier than now → 20001 `data.fields=[published_at]` (编排者默认); a later time schedules
the version, which counts as unpublished until then (04 §6.2). The save checks of POST
/admin/v1/articles run again with the same `data.fields`. Older published versions stay
published; the current version is the largest published version already due. An article
of category agreement → 20001 `data.fields=[category]`. CAS: `expected_row_version` is the
article's `row_version` the console showed; publishing adds 1 to the newest row's
row_version in the same transaction, so a stale request, including a retry of one that
already took effect, never matches again: a mismatch → 20902 with `data.resource=article`.
An article_id that is not a lowercase canonical UUID, or that does not exist → 30701.
Written to the audit log in the same transaction.

scheduled.summary: Publish version 3 at a set time

post.summary: Take a whole article offline
post.description:
Permission point `content.article`. Sets every published version of the article,
scheduled ones not yet due included, to offline; drafts are not touched (04 §6.2「整篇下线」;
编排者默认 for drafts). An article with no published version → 20001
`data.fields=[article_id]`. For a notice, the time it was taken offline is recorded as
notice_end_at (BR-TEXT-13). An article of category agreement → 20001
`data.fields=[category]`. CAS: `expected_row_version` is the article's `row_version` the
console showed; going offline adds 1 to the newest row's row_version in the same
transaction; a mismatch → 20902 with `data.resource=article`. An article_id that is not a
lowercase canonical UUID, or that does not exist → 30701. Written to the audit log in the
same transaction.

get.summary: Dictionary keys with their bundled default and current text
get.description:
Permission point: any of `config.general`, `content.fund_terms` or `content.agreement`
(04 §11.2; read only, no step-up). One row per key of contracts/texts.default.json (the
keys the dictionary may override, 编排者默认), in key order, page by page (`page`,
`page_size` ≤ 200), optionally narrowed by `class` and `key_prefix`: the key's class (which
permission point writes it, BR-TEXT-12 细则: `fund_terms` = a fund term key, `agreement`
= privacy and permission texts of table D (`privacy.`, `perm.`), `general` = every other
key), the bundled default, the current override (null = the bundled default applies) and
the version of the key's current row (null = never written). `dict_version` is the
dictionary's current version ("0" before the first publish), the `expected_version` of
the writes.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Only keys of this class.

parameters.name: key_prefix
parameters.description: Only keys starting with this text.

put.description:
Saving publishes (no separate draft step, 编排者默认): the changed keys take effect as a new
dictionary version (BR-TEXT-12 细则). One request changes keys of one class only, and the
class picks the permission point and step-up (04 §11.2, BR-ID-34): `general` →
`config.general`, no step-up; `fund_terms` → `content.fund_terms`, totp tier every time;
`agreement` → `content.agreement`, totp tier, and `legal_confirmed_by` is required. Keys
of more than one class → 20001 with `data.fields=[changes]`; lacking the class's point →
10403 with `data.reason=admin_permission_denied`; without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` where needed → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`. A key the server cannot
classify counts as a fund term key (BR-TEXT-12 细则). Every change is checked first, and
any failure is 20001 with nothing saved: a key not in contracts/texts.default.json, a key
listed twice, or a text equal to the current one → `data.fields` names
`changes[<i>].key`; a text whose variables (`{name}` placeholders) differ from the
bundled default's, or that contains a forbidden word → `data.fields` names
`changes[<i>].text` followed by the forbidden words found; an `agreement` change without
`legal_confirmed_by` → `data.fields=[legal_confirmed_by]`. Only then is
`expected_version` compared with the current dictionary version, and a mismatch is 20902
with `data.resource=dict_item` and nothing saved (04 §6.6). On success every changed key
gets a new row (text null = back to the bundled default) at the new version (current
plus 1), dict_version moves to it in the same transaction, and the audit log records
the keys with before and after texts, whether they are fund terms and the legal
confirmer. Clients see the change when their GET /v1/dict cache refreshes. No
Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

200.description: The new dictionary version and the keys written.

get.summary: Version history of dictionary keys
get.description:
Permission point: any of `config.general`, `content.fund_terms` or `content.agreement`
(04 §11.2; read only, no step-up). Every stored dictionary row, newest first (by version,
then key), page by page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200), optionally for one `key`: the key, the
dictionary version it was written at, its text (null = back to the bundled default), who
wrote it and when. Rows are never changed; a rollback adds new rows (POST
/admin/v1/dict-items/rollback).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Only the rows of this key.

200.description: One page of dictionary rows, newest first.

post.summary: Roll dictionary keys back to an older dictionary version
post.description:
Writes, for every key in `keys`, the text the key had at dictionary version `to_version`
(its newest row at or below that version; none, or `to_version` 0 → null, back to the
bundled default) as a new row at a new dictionary version (current plus 1); history is
never rewritten (BR-TEXT-12 细则). Classes, permission point, step-up and
`legal_confirmed_by` as for PUT /admin/v1/dict-items (one class per request: `general` →
`config.general`, no step-up; `fund_terms` → `content.fund_terms`, totp tier;
`agreement` → `content.agreement`, totp tier and `legal_confirmed_by`; mixed classes →
20001 with `data.fields=[keys]`; lacking the point → 10403; without a valid totp-tier
`X-Step-Up-Token` where needed → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). Checked first, with nothing
written on failure (20001): `to_version` not lower than the current dictionary version →
`data.fields=[to_version]`; a key not in contracts/texts.default.json or listed twice →
`data.fields` names `keys[<i>]`; a restored text that no longer passes the variable or
forbidden-word check → `data.fields` names `keys[<i>]` followed by the forbidden words
found. Then CAS: `expected_version` is the current dictionary version, and a mismatch is
20902 with `data.resource=dict_item`. Audited like a save. No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

200.description: The new dictionary version and the keys written.

get.summary: Registered emergency switches and their current values
get.description:
Permission point: any of `switch.all`, `switch.payout` or `switch.pay` (04 §11.2; read
only, no step-up). One row per switch the server has registered (04 §10.2, one row per
concrete key such as `convert.enabled.taobao`), in registry order, page by page (`page`,
`page_size` ≤ 200): the current value (null = never written, the registered `default`
applies), the value type and, for `enum`, the allowed values, the permission points of
which any one may change it (`permissions`), whether the console may change it at all
(`admin_editable`; false for `agent.whitelist_only` and `agent.model_route`; true for
`withdraw.auto_payout.enabled` means it can only be turned off, `true` is refused), and the
`version` that PUT /admin/v1/kill-switches/{key} takes as `expected_version`. Rows the
account may not change are still listed, so the console can show them read only.

put.description:
Permission point by key (04 §11.2), any one of the listed points suffices:
`withdraw.enabled`, `payout.enabled`, `payout.queue_paused`,
`payout.channel_enabled.<channel>` and `payout.channel_paused.<channel>` need
`switch.all` or `switch.payout`; `pay.enabled` and `pay.channel_enabled.<pay_channel>`
need `switch.all` or `switch.pay`; every other switch, `withdraw.auto_payout.enabled`
included, needs `switch.all`. Lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. `withdraw.auto_payout.enabled` can only be turned
off from the console (BR-WDR-30: off is the safe direction): `false` follows the rules
here, `true` is 20001 with `data.fields=[value]`; turning it on needs the owner's
confirmation, a separate flow outside this operation. Step-up: totp tier for every key, clearing
`payout.queue_paused` and `payout.channel_paused.<channel>` included (04 §11.2, BR-ID-34):
without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`.
A key the server has not registered, or one the console may not change
(`agent.whitelist_only`, `agent.model_route`; `admin_editable=false`), is 20001 with
`data.fields=[key]`; a value of the wrong type or outside `options` is 20001 with
`data.fields=[value]`. CAS: `expected_version` is the switch's `version` the console
showed (0 for a switch never written); every change adds 1 and a mismatch → 20902 with
`data.resource=kill_switch`, refresh and retry (04 §6.6). Writing the value the switch
already has with a matching version succeeds without change, version bump, audit or
alert. `reason` is optional (at most 200 characters) and kept in the audit record.
Every change is written to the audit log (action kill_switch_change, before and after
values) and pushes an alert; it takes effect on every server instance within 10 seconds
(04 §10.2). No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

maintenance.summary: Mark the pdd conversion stop as maintenance (first write)

200.description: The switch as it is now.

get.summary: Registered configuration items and their current values
get.description:
Permission point: any of `config.general`, `config.risk` or `config.business` (04 §11.2;
read only, no step-up). One row per configuration key the server has registered (04 §10),
in registry order, page by page (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200): the current value (null =
never written, the server's built-in default applies), the value type and, for `enum`,
the allowed values, the permission point that guards changing it (`permission`), whether
the console may change it (`admin_editable`; false for `agent.page_guide.routes` and
`external_hosts` until their editors ship) and the `version` that the writes take as
`expected_version`. Emergency switches (04 §10.2) are not here but under
/admin/v1/kill-switches.

200.description: One page of registered configuration items.

post.summary: Change several configuration items at once
post.description:
Permission point: the one point that guards every key of the batch (`config.general`,
`config.risk` or `config.business`, 04 §11.2); a batch mixing keys of different points
is 20001 with `data.fields=[items]`, as is a key listed twice. Step-up by that point
(04 §11.2, BR-ID-34): none for `config.general`; totp tier for `config.risk` and
`config.business` (without a valid totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with
`data.tier=totp`). The whole batch takes effect or nothing does (05 F1-10): first every
key and value is checked (unregistered or not admin-editable keys, values of the wrong
type, outside `options` or failing the key's own rule such as the candidate set of
BR-AI-01 细则「页面引导」), and any failure is 20001 with `data.fields` listing every
failing key; only then are the versions compared, and any mismatch is 20902 with
`data.resource=config_item` and nothing applied. Each changed key gets its version plus
1, a history version and an audit record (action config_item_change) carrying the
shared `reason`; the change pushes an alert. Values take effect as each key's reader
re-reads it (within that key's cache period), never retroactively (04 §10). No
Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

200.description: Every item of the batch as it is now, in request order.

get.summary: One configuration item

put.description:
Permission point: the point that guards the key (its `permission`: `config.general`,
`config.risk` or `config.business`, 04 §11.2); lacking it is 10403 with
`data.reason=admin_permission_denied`. Step-up by that point (04 §11.2, BR-ID-34): none
for `config.general`; totp tier for `config.risk` and `config.business` (without a valid
totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). A key the server has not
registered, or one the console may not change (`admin_editable=false`:
`agent.page_guide.routes`, `external_hosts`), is 20001 with `data.fields=[key]`; a value
of the wrong type, outside `options` or failing the key's own rule is 20001 with
`data.fields=[value]`. CAS: `expected_version` is the item's `version` the console showed
(0 for an item never written); a change adds 1 and stores a history version, and a
mismatch → 20902 with `data.resource=config_item`, refresh and retry (04 §6.6). Writing
the value the item already has with a matching version succeeds without change. `reason`
is optional (at most 200 characters) and kept with the history version. Every change is
written to the audit log (action config_item_change, before and after values) and
pushes an alert; it takes effect as the key's reader re-reads it (within that key's
cache period), never retroactively (04 §10). No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

200.description: The configuration item as it is now.

get.summary: Version history of one configuration item
get.description:
Permission point: any of `config.general`, `config.risk` or `config.business` (04 §11.2;
read only, no step-up). Every stored version of the item, newest first, page by page
(`page`, `page_size` ≤ 200), with the value, who wrote it (null = written by the system)
and the reason given; any older version can be restored with POST
/admin/v1/config-items/{key}/rollback. A key the server has not registered is 20001 with
`data.fields=[key]`.

200.description: One page of versions, newest first.

post.summary: Roll one configuration item back to an older version
post.description:
Permission point and step-up as for PUT /admin/v1/config-items/{key}: the key's point
(`config.general`, `config.risk` or `config.business`, 04 §11.2); totp tier for
`config.risk` and `config.business`, none for `config.general` (without a valid
totp-tier `X-Step-Up-Token` → 10003 with `data.tier=totp`). Writes the value of
`to_version` as a new version (the current version plus 1); history is never rewritten.
`to_version` must be a stored version lower than the current one, otherwise 20001 with
`data.fields=[to_version]`; the restored value is checked against the key's current rule
like a new value (for example the candidate set of BR-AI-01 细则「页面引导」 for
`agent.page_guide.routes`), and a value that no longer passes is 20001 with
`data.fields=[to_version]` and nothing changes. An unregistered or not admin-editable key
is 20001 with `data.fields=[key]`. CAS: `expected_version` is the item's current
`version`; a mismatch → 20902 with `data.resource=config_item`. Written to the audit log
(action config_item_rollback) and pushes an alert; takes effect like a change (04 §10).
No Idempotency-Key (04 §6.6).

200.description: The configuration item with the restored value as its new version.

post.summary: Start a new conversation
post.description:
Owner per BR-AI-20: with an access token the user (any device); without one this device
(X-Device-Id), guest sessions only. Returns the owner's newest unexpired session while it
has no turn yet, otherwise creates one, so repeating the call never piles up empty sessions
(no Idempotency-Key, 04 §5 幂等). After BR-ID-01 ①–⑦ the checks of BR-AI-23 ①–③ apply:
30501 (agent.enabled / whitelist, BR-AI-12) → 10001 or 10005 (the switches of BR-ID-03) →
10004 with consent_type=ai_third_party (BR-AI-13; nothing is created). x-auth is optional
although 04 §6.5 lists none, for the same reason as search and consents.
Version gate: applied.

200.description: The new session, or the owner's newest empty one.

get.summary: The current conversation
get.description:
The owner's most recently active unexpired session, or session=null (BR-AI-20; owner as in
createAgentSession, a token never falls back to the device's guest sessions). The app opens
it on start; there is no session list (拍板第二批 AI-23). Checks BR-AI-23 ①–③: 30501 →
10001 / 10005 → 10004.

get.summary: Conversation history
get.description:
The messages of one session (04 §6.5 会话历史响应的形状, 2026-10-14). After BR-ID-01 ①–⑦
the checks of BR-AI-23 ①–④ apply in order: 30501 (agent.enabled / whitelist, BR-AI-12) →
10001 / 10005 (BR-ID-03) → 10004 consent_type=ai_third_party (BR-AI-13) → 30504 without
data when the session does not exist or the caller is not its owner (never told apart,
BR-AI-20; owner as in createAgentSession).
An expired session (BR-AI-20) is not an error here: its owner still gets 200 with
data.expired=true and the history is read-only (sending to it is 30504 on POST); an
unexpired session has data.expired=false.
Paging: the first page holds the newest `limit` messages; items[] inside a page are in time
order, oldest first. next_cursor fetches the page of earlier (older) messages; null means
there are no earlier messages.
Each item is one agent_messages row: role user (the text as the user sent it, cards [] and
finish_reason null) or assistant (the text after OutputGuard, possibly '' while nothing
has been written yet; finish_reason as in the done frame, contracts/enums agent_finish_reason,
null while the run has not ended). cards[] are the card frames as they were sent (card_id,
type, schema_version, data, fallback_text; the frame's seq is not kept); data follows
contracts/agent-stream.schema.json card_<type>, and a client that does not know the type
shows fallback_text (03 §7.4). One exception: earnings_summary keeps no amounts (BR-AI-19,
BR-AI-01 细则「收益查询」), so its data is only the earnings_summary_history shape, as_of and
the two action buttons (actions), and the client shows the history note instead of
reloading amounts. Not replayed: tool.status, ping, suggestions and meta frames. Product
cards keep quoted_at / age_sec and are aged by BR-PRICE-11; there is no extra field.
After a duplicate client_msg_id response or a disconnect the client reloads this list
(04 §8.1, 03 §7.2).

200.description: A page of messages, oldest first within the page.

active.summary: An unexpired session with earlier messages; a page guide and an earnings card

post.summary: Send a message; the reply is an SSE stream
post.description:
After BR-ID-01 ①–⑦, BR-AI-23 decides in this order and returns the first failure as the JSON
error envelope (Content-Type application/json, HTTP status per contracts/error-codes.yaml):
① 30501 (agent.enabled / whitelist, BR-AI-12) → ② 10001 / 10005 (BR-ID-03) → ③ 10004
consent_type=ai_third_party (BR-AI-13) → ④ 30504 without data (session missing, not the
caller's, or expired; BR-AI-20) → ⑤ 20001 data.fields=[text] when text is too long
(BR-AI-23 ⑤, counted in Unicode code points; checked here, not by the schema) → ⑥ repeated
client_msg_id: the two-frame stream below; ⑦–⑩ are not checked (only finishing a leftover
run of this session can still end it with JSON 50401 or 50001, see below) → ⑦ 30506 (a run
of this session is in progress) → ⑧ 42901 with Retry-After → ⑨ 30504
data.reason=round_limit → ⑩ 30502 data.reset_at, data.next (BR-AI-15). Only a request
passing ⑩ is counted.
A malformed body (types, client_msg_id format, unknown fields) is 20001 before ①.
Before acceptance (BR-AI-23 细则 受理结果不明 / 谁来收尾, 2026-10-08), two more JSON errors:
JSON 50401 when the store is unavailable or the outcome of the acceptance transaction is
unknown (the lookup by client_msg_id is still unclear); not counting the message is not
guaranteed, so the client retries with the same client_msg_id and ⑥ gives the definite
result. JSON 50001 when a leftover run of this session is pending manual handling (its data
cannot be finished automatically); this is decided before ⑦ (before "a run is in progress")
and the client guides the user to a new session. Both ⑥ and ⑦ first finish (settle and
write the terminal state of) a leftover run of this session in their own acceptance
transaction; when that finishing hits an unavailable store or an unknown outcome the answer
is JSON 50401, and when the leftover run is pending manual handling it is JSON 50001.
Accepted: 200 text/event-stream; each event is one frame of
contracts/agent-stream.schema.json (`event:` / `id:` / `data:` lines, a `: ping` comment
every 15 s); meta first, exactly one terminal frame (done or error) last. Failures after
acceptance are error frames (30501 when the switch goes off, 10004 when the consent is
withdrawn, 50302 with fallback_q, 50001, 50401). No resume (02 §9): after a disconnect the
client reloads GET .../messages (03 §7.2). The client tells the two kinds of answer apart by
Content-Type.
Repeated client_msg_id (⑥, 04 §8.1 重复消息; the body is not compared): when it is answered
with a stream, 200 text/event-stream with two frames, ids from 1: meta (the original run's
ids, duplicate=true) and the original terminal frame replayed (an original run with no
terminal state that is not running is finished first, then replayed), or error 30506
(retryable, fallback and fallback_q null) while the original run is still running. If
finishing the original run hits an unavailable store or an unknown outcome, ⑥ returns
JSON 50401 instead (retry with the same client_msg_id); if the original run is pending
manual handling, JSON 50001, decided before the still-running check.
context comes from the entry points of 01 §4 (商品详情、剪贴板提示条、订单详情) and is
handled like tool input (an order_id that is not the caller's is not found, BR-AI-07).
Version gate: applied.

schema.description: Server-sent events; one event is one AgentStreamFrame of contracts/agent-stream.schema.json.

accepted.summary: An accepted message answered with one page guide card

duplicateEnded.summary: A repeated client_msg_id whose run has ended

duplicateInProgress.summary: A repeated client_msg_id whose run is still running

post.summary: Stop generating
post.description:
Stops a running reply (BR-AI-23 细则 取消, 2026-10-08). Checks BR-AI-23 ①–③. A repeated call
for a run already cancelled by this endpoint (its cancel recorded; the run not yet ended or
ended as cancelled) returns 200 again and writes nothing. Otherwise 30505 when the run does
not exist, is not in a session of the caller (never told apart), has ended, already has an
end reason written on the run row, or is past its deadline (accepted time + the longest run
duration, BR-AI-14); the deadline is judged by the server time after the run row is locked.
Otherwise the cancel is written on the run row and the call returns 200; a 200 guarantees
that the run ends with finish_reason=cancelled, which is counted (BR-AI-15). Version gate:
applied.

post.summary: Thumbs up or down on a reply
post.description:
Writes agent_messages.feedback of the message (04 §6.5); down marks the run as a badcase
(BR-AI-19). A malformed body (feedback missing or not up / down, unknown fields) is 20001.
After BR-ID-01 ①–⑦ the checks of BR-AI-23 ①–③ apply: 30501 → 10001 / 10005 → 10004; then
30504 without data when the message does not exist or its session is not the caller's
(never told apart, BR-AI-20). Version gate: applied.

post.summary: Report a reply
post.description:
Writes agent_messages.reported and report_reason (04 §6.5, BR-AI-19). reason is free text
of 1–200 characters: 08 has not fixed a set of report reasons, so the contract has no enum
for it. A malformed body (reason missing, empty or too long, unknown fields) is 20001.
After BR-ID-01 ①–⑦ the checks of BR-AI-23 ①–③ apply: 30501 → 10001 / 10005 → 10004; then
30504 without data when the message does not exist or its session is not the caller's
(never told apart, BR-AI-20). Version gate: applied.

bearerAuth.description:
`Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`; ES256 JWT with uid, app_id, sid, device_id, scp,
valid 2 hours (BR-ID-07). After login app_id is taken from the token only.

adminBearerAuth.description:
`Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>` on every /admin/v1 operation after login (CT-02f).
admin_token is a JWT signed with its own key (aud=admin, not accepted on /v1), valid
8 hours and expiring after 30 minutes without activity (BR-ID-34); expired or idle → 10001
without reason. The console keeps it only in memory and sessionStorage and sends it only in
this header; it is never a cookie, so requests carry no ambient credential and need no
CSRF token. The admin API allows CORS only from the exact admin console origin (02 §3.4).
The step-up token of an operation goes in the `X-Step-Up-Token` header (04 §5).

AppId.name: X-App-Id
AppId.description: App (brand) the request belongs to; before login it must match the app_id the device was registered with (10403, BR-ID-07).

AppVersion.name: X-App-Version
AppVersion.description: SemVer, the same number on all three apps (拍板第二批 TECH-07).

Channel.name: X-Channel
Channel.description: Install channel of the app package (enum install_channel); absent for H5.

TraceId.name: X-Trace-Id
TraceId.description: Client-generated trace id, echoed as `trace_id` when well-formed.

DeviceId.name: X-Device-Id
DeviceId.description: device_id issued by POST /v1/devices; anything else is 10402 (BR-ID-09).

OptionalDeviceId.name: X-Device-Id
OptionalDeviceId.description: device_id issued by POST /v1/devices, when the device is registered.

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: The ETag of the client's last good response (LKG); a match gets 304.

Nonce.name: X-Nonce
Nonce.description: 32 lowercase hex characters; (device_id, nonce) unique within 600 s (BR-ID-09).

Sign.name: X-Sign
Sign.description:
lowercase_hex(HMAC-SHA256(install_secret, METHOD + "
" + path with raw query + "
" + ts
+ "
" + nonce + "
" + lowercase_hex(sha256(raw body)))) (BR-ID-09).

StepUpToken.name: X-Step-Up-Token
StepUpToken.description:
step_up_token from POST /v1/auth/step-up for the operation's x-step-up action (04 §5). Missing,
expired or for another action → 10003 (not 20001; that is why the header is optional).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Required on operations marked I (04 §6); missing → 20001. Same key while processing →
40901; same key with another body → 20901; a retry after a timeout reuses the key and gets
the first result (拍板第二批 TRADE-22). On the x-step-up operations a key abandoned through
POST /v1/idempotency-keys/abandon → 20903, without comparing the body (04 §5「幂等」).

does not own the attempt_id in the body, is 20001 with data.fields=[attempt_id] (no 30144).

LinkId.description: link_id from a card; unknown or of another app → 30144.

A configuration or emergency-switch key as registered by the server (04 §10, §10.2), dotted
and concrete (`convert.enabled.taobao`, not `convert.enabled.<platform>`); an unregistered

ProductOk.summary: Detail card with a fresh link_id
